subject.title: Native Slack token rotation support (oauth.v2.access refresh flow)

question: Should the bundled Slack plugin own native Slack OAuth token rotation now, and where should refresh tokens, client secrets, expiry metadata, and refreshed bot tokens be stored and adopted at runtime?
rationale: The feature is feasible and aligned with Slack security needs, but it creates new persistent credential state and active auth mutation that automation should not define without maintainer product and security direction.

options.title: Design native Slack rotation
options.body: Keep this issue open and require a maintainer-approved Slack plugin design for secure storage, transactional refresh, runtime adoption, status/doctor UX, docs, and live Slack validation.

options.title: Keep rotation external for now
options.body: Document the current static-token model and supported reload path if maintainers decide OpenClaw should not own rotating Slack OAuth material yet.

options.title: Wait for generic rotating credentials
options.body: Defer implementation until OpenClaw has a shared plugin credential-refresh/storage API that Slack can consume without one-off config state.

recommendation.title: Design native Slack rotation
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and require a maintainer-approved Slack plugin design for secure storage, transactional refresh, runtime adoption, status/doctor UX, docs, and live Slack validation.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current blame and issue-timeline signals point to @steipete for Slack credential/runtime direction.
